questions.stem: Peak effect of an IV thiopental induction dose?
questions.explanation: Thiopental, peak: 30–60 sec. 3–5 min is midazolam's peak. 5–8 min is thiopental's duration. 10–15 min is dexmedetomidine's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of an IV etomidate induction dose?
questions.explanation: Etomidate, peak: 60 sec. 4–8 min is etomidate's duration. 10–15 min is dexmedetomidine's onset. 3–5 min is midazolam's peak. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of an IV ketamine induction dose?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, IV peak: 60 sec. 10–20 min is hydromorphone's peak. 3–5 min is midazolam's peak. 5–10 min is ketamine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of IV lidocaine given at induction?
questions.explanation: Lidocaine IV, peak: 1–2 min. 20–30 sec is faster than lidocaine reaches its peak. 5–10 min is too late for an IV bolus. 10–20 min is IV lidocaine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of succinylcholine at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, peak: 60 sec. 4–6 min is succinylcholine's duration. 3–5 min is vecuronium and cisatracurium peak. 2–3 min is vecuronium's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of cisatracurium at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Cisatracurium, peak: 3–5 min. 60 sec is succinylcholine's peak. ~55 min is cisatracurium's duration. 1–3 min is rocuronium's peak. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of IV glycopyrrolate?
questions.explanation: Glycopyrrolate, peak: 5 min. 1 min is glycopyrrolate's onset. 30 min is too late. 2–3 hr is glycopyrrolate's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of IV atropine?
questions.explanation: Atropine, peak: 2–4 min. 30–60 min is atropine's duration. 10–15 min is too late. 1 min is atropine's onset. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of an IV phenylephrine bolus?
questions.explanation: Phenylephrine, peak: 1 min. 2–5 min is ephedrine's peak. 10–15 min is too late. 5–10 min is phenylephrine's duration. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Peak effect of an IV ephedrine bolus?
questions.explanation: Ephedrine, peak: 2–5 min. <1 min is ephedrine's onset. 20–30 min is too late. 10 min is ephedrine's duration on the sheet. Source: USAGPAN reference sheet.

questions.stem: Onset of IV alfentanil, the fastest of the fentanyl family?
questions.explanation: Alfentanil, onset: ~1 min. 10–15 min is hydromorphone's onset. 3–5 min is fentanyl's peak. 5–14 min is morphine's onset. Source: Standard references (Stoelting's Pharmacology).

questions.stem: Onset of IV naloxone?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, onset: 1–2 min. 10–15 min is too slow for IV naloxone. 5–14 min is morphine's onset. 30–45 min is naloxone's duration. Source: Naloxone labeling.

questions.stem: Onset of IV flumazenil?
questions.explanation: Flumazenil, onset: 1–2 min. 5 seconds is faster than flumazenil acts. 30–60 min is a typical duration of effect. 10–15 min is too slow for IV flumazenil. Source: Flumazenil labeling.

questions.stem: Onset of IV edrophonium?
questions.explanation: Edrophonium, onset: 1–2 min. 10–15 sec is faster than edrophonium acts. 7–10 min is closer to neostigmine's peak. 30 min is too slow. Source: Standard references.

questions.stem: Onset of IM ketamine?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, IM onset: 3–8 min. 15–30 min is too slow for IM ketamine. 1 min is closer to IV onset. 30–60 sec is the IV onset. Source: Ketamine labeling.

questions.stem: Time for oral midazolam premedication to take effect in a child?
questions.explanation: Midazolam, oral onset: 20–30 min. 1–2 min is the IV onset. 3–5 min is the IV peak. 60–90 min is too slow. Source: Standard pediatric anesthesia references.

questions.stem: Onset of IV metoclopramide?
questions.explanation: Metoclopramide, IV onset: 1–3 min. 15–20 min is slower than IV metoclopramide. 4–8 hr is dexamethasone's full antiemetic onset. 30–60 min is closer to the oral onset. Source: Metoclopramide labeling.

questions.stem: Duration of IV naloxone?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, duration: 30–45 min. 10–15 min is too brief. 6–8 hr is far longer than naloxone lasts. 2–4 hr is morphine's duration. Source: Naloxone labeling.

questions.stem: Clinical duration of pancuronium at an intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Pancuronium, duration: 60–90 min. 30–45 min is an intermediate relaxant's duration. 3–4 hr is longer than pancuronium lasts. 4–6 min is succinylcholine's duration. Source: Pancuronium labeling.

questions.stem: Duration of IV meperidine?
questions.explanation: Meperidine, duration: 2–4 hr. 3–10 min is remifentanil's duration. 8–12 hr is closer to methadone. 30–60 min is fentanyl's duration. Source: Standard references.

questions.stem: Duration of analgesia from intrathecal morphine?
questions.explanation: Morphine, intrathecal duration: 12–24 hr. 2–4 hr is IV morphine's duration. 1–4 hr is closer to intrathecal fentanyl. 48–72 hr is longer than intrathecal morphine lasts. Source: SOAP and standard obstetric anesthesia references.

questions.stem: Duration of analgesia from intrathecal fentanyl?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, intrathecal duration: 1–4 hr. 10–20 min is too brief. 30–60 sec is its onset scale, not duration. 12–24 hr is intrathecal morphine's duration. Source: Standard obstetric anesthesia references.

questions.stem: Duration of IV ketorolac?
questions.explanation: Ketorolac, duration: 4–6 hr. 1–2 hr is shorter than ketorolac lasts. 12–24 hr is too long. 30–60 min is too brief. Source: Ketorolac labeling.

questions.stem: Duration of IV hydralazine?
questions.explanation: Hydralazine, duration: 2–4 hr. 24 hr is longer than usual. 10–30 min is esmolol's duration. 5–10 min is phenylephrine's duration. Source: Standard references.

questions.stem: Concentration of 1.5% mepivacaine?

questions.explanation: Dobutamine premix (250 mg/250 mL): 1,000 mcg/mL. 16 mcg/mL is a norepinephrine infusion. 200 mcg/mL is premixed milrinone. 1,600 mcg/mL is premixed dopamine. Source: Standard premix.

questions.explanation: Dopamine premix (400 mg/250 mL): 1,600 mcg/mL. 1,000 mcg/mL is premixed dobutamine. 200 mcg/mL is premixed milrinone. 400 mcg/mL is 400 mg in 1,000 mL. Source: Standard premix.

questions.stem: Concentration of IV diltiazem?

questions.stem: Concentration of 25% mannitol?
